title: LionGate holds Flowable Strategic status but positions on CX transformation, not OSS
content:
LionGate AG carries Flowable Strategic status and describes itself as a system integrator, but its market positioning is customer-experience transformation rather than open-source conviction. The record's instruction is to verify before pitching, which makes this a flagged row rather than a scored one.

The distinction the flag protects is between a certification and a posture. Strategic tier says the firm has invested in a relationship with Flowable; it says nothing about whether the firm's architecture defaults are client-owned and open, or whether it would carry that argument into a client conversation. A CX-transformation practice typically sells journeys and front-end outcomes, where the record-keeping layer underneath is an implementation detail chosen for convenience — often a managed proprietary service.

This is the same failure mode the corpus flags in other forms: Incentro had good open-source posture but hyperscaler anchoring, and several rows carry an explicit instruction to run an OSS-portfolio screen before acting. A high partner tier is the easiest signal to acquire and the weakest predictor of posture, so it should never substitute for the screen. Provenance: Flowable Partner Finder, mined 2026-08-18, not imprint-swept.
